﻿Hey — hit this hard on Windows with OpenCode 1.18.3 (xAI grok-4.5).

What we saw:
- 5 short parallel Task subagents (write a tiny file and exit) → all 5 finish fine
- 5 long parallel Task subagents (multi-minute code review style work) → some get killed mid-flight
- Log shows `message=cancel` then `error=Aborted stack=undefined` on the children
- Parent just gets "Task cancelled"

So it's not a hard "max 3 agents" limit — short ones survive, long ones die. Matches what you described: one bad/stuck path takes siblings down with it.

We filed a fuller write-up with repro steps here: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/37959
(the bot there pointed us at this issue as the main one — +1 from us)

Happy to pull more logs or retest on a fix build if useful.

+1 with an independent headless reproduction on **OpenCode 1.17.18** using **`zai-coding-plan/glm-5.1`**.

We run OpenCode through `opencode serve` as a benchmark backend. On a real coding task, we have **12 persisted runs: 5 successes and 7 failures**. Every one of the 7 failures has the same signature:

- no final assistant result;
- no tool-created artifact;
- non-zero provider usage;
- `output_tokens + reasoning_tokens = 32,000` exactly;
- reasoning consumes almost the entire budget (31,933–31,987 tokens);
- the session then reaches idle/terminal state without a usable result.

Persisted failure samples:

| elapsed | output | reasoning | completion |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 915.1s | 33 | 31,967 | **32,000** |
| 357.6s | 36 | 31,964 | **32,000** |
| 470.1s | 61 | 31,939 | **32,000** |

We repeated the same task twice with `--no-save`; both failed again at exactly 32,000 completion tokens:

- 457.1s: output 33 + reasoning 31,967;
- 517.7s: output 29 + reasoning 31,971.

Control prompts on the same provider/model succeed quickly (`hello_world` in 21.9s, `fast_sort` in 19.4s), so this is not a general provider outage. We also saw no `ECONNRESET`, malformed SSE, or network error in these failures.

Our wrapper currently reports this as a hung `POST /message`, but that is misleading: the provider clearly returned usage. The actual failure is consistent with the 32k per-step cap being exhausted by reasoning and OpenCode ending the turn without exposing/recovering from `finish_reason=length`.

One important operational detail: successful and failed run durations overlap substantially (successes 515–1,077s; failures 358–915s), so a wall-clock watchdog cannot reliably identify this condition. Preserving and surfacing the terminal finish reason would let headless callers fail immediately and accurately; auto-continuation or an explicit actionable output-limit error would be even better.

Full local reproduction data and proposed downstream handling: https://github.com/axisrow/llm_benchmark/issues/161

Thanks for the review! While #27892 and #24981 are related, this proposal goes significantly further.

**Key Difference -- Full Lifecycle Automation:**

| | #27892 / #24981 | **This Proposal (#37993)** |
|---|---|---|
| Approach | Passive: respect system proxy or add static config field | **Active: automated workflow** |
| Proxy startup | User must manually start proxy | **OpenCode auto-starts proxy core** |
| Core integration | None | **Built-in Mihomo/Clash core launcher** |
| Subscription | N/A | **Auto-download subscription config** |
| Cleanup | User manually stops | **Auto-shutdown after task complete** |

**Workflow:**
Network timeout -> auto-detect -> download subscription -> start Mihomo core -> set proxy -> retry request -> task done -> auto stop

The existing issues just add a config field for an already-running proxy. This proposal lets OpenCode manage the entire proxy lifecycle automatically.

Happy to move this to #27892 if preferred, but the auto-start/stop workflow deserves dedicated consideration.

**Reference:** https://github.com/tianshan233/auto-proxy

Follow-up with a live A/B run and downstream mitigation on **OpenCode 1.17.18** with **`zai-coding-plan/glm-5.1`**, using the same real coding prompt and cleared proxy variables:

| mode | elapsed | input | output | reasoning | aggregate completion | result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| default 32k ceiling | 596.0s | 45,650 | 9,029 | 26,298 | 35,327 | success + artifact |
| `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX=65536` | 959.9s | 66,072 | 11,689 | 51,094 | 62,783 | success + artifact |

The default run happened to succeed this time, which is consistent with the stochastic behavior in the earlier sample: nine independent failures ended at exactly 32,000 completion tokens, while other runs succeeded.

With the 65,536 override, the OpenCode log shows the initial build step running for about **784 seconds before the first tool action**, after which the agent wrote the artifact and completed. The 62,783 figure is aggregate completion usage for the full run, not proof that one step consumed all of it; nevertheless, this successful run is consistent with the higher ceiling avoiding the repeatedly observed 32k termination.

We also implemented downstream handling in the benchmark wrapper:
- expose an explicit output-token ceiling;
- preserve and surface terminal `finish=length` / `MessageOutputLengthError`;
- stop waiting for a missing `session.idle` once terminal length is observed;
- optional first-action watchdog.

A live watchdog smoke test with a 5s threshold exited this workload in **34.1s** instead of waiting 10–20 minutes. The current floor is the existing 30s `POST /message` read timeout.

Details and test results: https://github.com/axisrow/llm_benchmark/issues/161

**Context:** Reconfirming this bug is still present in **v1.18.4** (latest, installed today). One new signal below that wasn't in the original report.

**Environment**
- OpenCode Desktop **1.18.4** (Electron 42.3.3 / Chromium 148), installed 2026-07-20 18:10
- OS: Windows 11
- Layout: **old layout** (`oldLayoutEligible: true`) — see "new signal" below
- Plugins: `plugin: []` (empty, ruled out)
- 5 active local worktrees
- Provider: opencode-go, model: MiniMax-M3

**Reproduction confirmed (this run, 2026-07-20 23:32 UTC)**
1. `C:\Users\ivo\AppData\Roaming\ai.opencode.desktop\logs\20260720T203241\`
2. `renderer.log`: 53 `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` lines in 344 s.
3. Peak burst: 16 errors in any 5 s window (avg 6.6 s between errors).
4. `main.log` clean: sidecar ready in 2.4 s, no errors.
5. `crash.log` and Crashpad empty — the renderer hangs, it does not crash.
6. 6–7 `OpenCode.exe` processes accumulate, the main process is ~320 MB RSS.
7. UI freezes on the "Thinking" indicator after a few minutes. Kill all `OpenCode.exe` + restart re-enables input.

**🆕 New signal not in the original report**

The original report scoped this to the v2 composer dock. I am on the **old layout** (`oldLayoutEligible: true` confirmed in `opencode.settings`), and I still see the same `ResizeObserver` flood plus the same UI freeze. This suggests the bug also exists in the legacy session page, not only in the new v2 composer. If your fix only touches the three `createResizeObserver` calls in the v2 composer, please also check whether the same or similar observer cluster exists in the legacy `packages/app/src/pages/session_legacy/` (or whatever the v1 code path is called).

**What I see in the wild that you might not see in your repro**
- The UI does not always show a "Thinking" indicator during the freeze. Sometimes the input box becomes completely unresponsive — I cannot click the send button, the model dropdown doesn't open, nothing. Other times the "Thinking" indicator is rendered but the model is not actually producing tokens (and re-sending the same message after restart shows the previous one was never sent at all — it was lost on freeze).
- The freeze is intermittent: I can send 2–3 messages successfully, then the next one hangs. Not every message is affected.
- This pattern is independent of model, session, or workspace. Repro: send image attachments + a multi-paragraph prompt.

**Temporary workaround I'm using**
1. When frozen: `taskkill /F /IM OpenCode.exe`, then restart. Re-send the lost message.
2. Lock window size after launch; do not resize (avoids triggering the observer chain).
3. Send a short "priming" message (e.g. a single character) within ~5 s of UI ready to anchor the layout before observers fire.

## Runtime-level lazy MCP resolution — transparent, zero round-trip

All current proposals (`mcp_search`, `mcp_load_tools`) put the burden on the agent: the agent has to (1) remember to search, (2) call a meta-tool, (3) wait until the next turn to actually use the tool. That is 2 turns to do 1 thing.

### The metadata is already there

During the MCP `initialize` handshake, servers send `serverInfo.name`, `serverInfo.version`, and several SDKs (`mcp-go`, `mcp-js`) already include `description` or `instructions` fields. Opencode receives this but discards it — instead injecting full tool schemas for every server.

### Proposal — 3 layers

**1. Minimal manifest in system prompt (~50 tokens)**

Instead of ~70k tokens of full schemas, inject only:

```
▶ playwright — Browser automation: navigate, click, snapshot
▶ supabase  — PostgreSQL DB: query, insert, schema management
▶ github    — Repo management: issues, PRs, code search
▶ figma     — Design components, export assets
▶ filesystem— File ops: read, write, search, glob
```

That is enough for the agent to decide which server it needs.

**2. Runtime lazy resolution (the core)**

The agent calls the tool directly:

`playwright__browser_navigate({ url: "https://..." })`

Opcodes intercepts, parses `server=playwright`, `tool=browser_navigate`, resolves the schema against the MCP server (or uses a cached `tools/list`), and injects it into the provider request **in the same turn**. No `mcp_search`, no extra round-trip, no lazy-loading awareness from the agent.

**3. Provider-level defer (future)**

When the provider supports it (Anthropic `defer_loading: true`, OpenAI tool_search), opencode sends all tools deferred and the provider expands the matching tool within the same request — zero server round-trips at all.

### Comparison

| Aspect | mcp_search (#12520) | Runtime resolution (this proposal) |
|--------|-------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Agent calls | 2 calls (search + tool) | 1 call (tool directly) |
| Turns to complete | 2 | 1 |
| Extra tokens | mcp_search invocation | 0 |
| Transparent to agent? | No | Yes |
| Uses server metadata? | No | Yes |
